$comment: Runtime form protocol v2 and v3: the single source for the TypeScript and Kotlin wire types. Edit this file, then run `pnpm --filter @botiverse/raft-runtime-form contract:generate`. Every type is open: receivers must ignore keys they do not know (README, Protocol v2 and Protocol v3).
name: RuntimeFormV2

Definition.doc: Response of GET /api/servers/:id/machines/:machineId/runtime-forms/v2/:runtimeId (create), or of GET /api/agents/:id/runtime-form (edit, with `values`: the agent's current field values; writeOnly fields are never included).

protocolVersion.doc: 2, or 3 when the request advertised `runtime_form.v3` (query `clientCapabilities`). A v2 parser rejects 3 (fail closed). v3 differs from v2 only in: `uiSchema.rules` instead of `uiSchema.visibility`, `dataSchema.allOf` conditional required, no `x-optionsFrom` (a reasoning effort is an `x-optionSource` dependent_select), no `x-connectionOwned` (a HIDE rule + conditional required), unavailable options only in `OptionSource.unavailableOptions` (never `Option.unavailable`), `revision` on every form, and `requiredClientCapabilities` empty (v3 implies the v2 names).

requiredClientCapabilities.doc: Client capabilities this form needs beyond the base v2 renderer. Absent or null means []. A client that sees an entry it does not implement, a value that is not an array, or a non-string entry must treat the whole v2 form as unavailable and fall back to its v1/legacy form; it must never render a partial v2 form. Names (frozen): `select.custom_value` (OptionSource.customValueAllowed), `choice.labels` (FieldCopy.choices), `option_source.status` (OptionSource.status/reason/retryable), `provider.saved_connection` (Option.connectionId/underlyingProviderId/group/unavailable: saved provider connection options in a provider source; the client must render the saved group, keep connection-owned fields (the writeOnly secret and any gateway URL/capability field) out of formValues entirely — never as empty strings — restore the direct schema's own visibility/required rules for them when the selection moves off a connection, and never submit an apiKey for a connection selection). A form lists a name only when it uses that feature; the server never sends those fields to a form that does not list the name.

revision.doc: Opaque token identifying this exact form build (entry version + relevant server flags + scope; on v3 also the saved connections named in rule conditions). Sent only on the v2/v3 form endpoints: on v2 only for saved-connection forms, on v3 on every form. A client that fetches option sources for this form should pass it back as ?formRevision=<token>; see OptionSource for the three outcomes. Clients that do not know it keep working: the parameter is optional.

writeOnlyKeepRequiresUnchanged.doc: Edit only (sent with `values`). Keyed by the pointer of a writeOnly field (e.g. `/apiKey`); the value lists the pointers of the fields the stored secret is bound to (e.g. `["/provider", "/apiUrl"]`). On edit a blank writeOnly field keeps the stored secret only while every listed field still equals its value in `values`. Comparison: both sides as strings (absent = ""), surrounding whitespace trimmed and trailing `/` characters removed, then exact. A listed field that is currently hidden by `visibility` is not compared. When a listed field differs and the secret is blank (and visible), the client must treat the secret as required and block saving, saying a new secret is needed; the server refuses that save anyway (`api_key_required` at the field). Absent: a blank writeOnly field always means keep. A secret pointer or listed pointer naming no field is ignored. Optional and advisory: no requiredClientCapabilities entry; a client that ignores it still gets the server's refusal.

allOf.doc: v3 only. Conditional required: each entry's `if` is a condition schema evaluated against the whole form values (Condition rules: supported keywords, absent value = ""); when it holds, the names in `then.required` are required, otherwise those in `else.required`. A field hidden by a rule is never required. Top-level `required` stays unconditional.

FieldSchema.doc: Render by `type` (with x-optionSource or x-optionsFrom), never by field name. An unknown `type` is unsupported: skip it if optional, block saving if required.

x-optionsFrom.doc: v2 only. On v3 a field whose choices follow another field's option is an `x-optionSource` dependent_select.

x-connectionOwned.doc: capability `provider.saved_connection`. True on a field whose value a selected saved provider connection owns (the writeOnly secret, a gateway URL/capability field). While the field that offers connection options holds a connection selection, a client renders this field disabled with a placeholder, treats it as not required, and keeps it out of formValues entirely (never an empty string); moving the selection off a connection restores this field's own visibility and required rules and clears its value. Sent only to forms that declare the capability. v2 only: v3 expresses the same with a HIDE rule and `dataSchema.allOf`.

additionalProperties.doc: JSON Schema allows a boolean (`false`) or a value schema (`{"type": "string"}` for a key-value map); clients must accept both.

OptionsFrom.doc: Choices derived from the option currently selected in another field: that option's `attribute` (a string list) are the choices, and its `defaultAttribute` (if any) is the default. Example: Kimi reasoning effort follows the selected model.

rules.doc: v3 only. At most one rule per field (compound conditions use condition.scope "#"). A field hidden by a rule is not validated, not required and not submitted.

VisibilityRule.doc: Show the field at `pointer` only when the field at when.pointer has one of when.in.

Rule.doc: v3: JSONForms-style rule for the field at `scope`.

scope.doc: The field the rule applies to: `#/properties/<key>`.

effect.doc: SHOW: visible only while the condition holds. HIDE: hidden while it holds. Any other effect is unsupported: the client treats the whole form as unavailable.

Condition.doc: v3: `schema` is evaluated against the value at `scope` (`#` = the whole values object, `#/properties/<key>` = one field). Supported keywords: const, enum (structural equality: object key order does not count), pattern (a portable ECMAScript subset, unanchored unless the pattern anchors; see the package README), not, anyOf, allOf, properties. An absent value is evaluated as "". A schema using any other keyword, or a pattern outside the subset, is unsupported: the client treats the whole form as unavailable (new keywords need a required client capability). packages/runtime-form/fixtures/v3.conditions.conformance.json is the conformance table every client runs.

choices.doc: capability `choice.labels`. Display copy for the choices of a `select` or `derived_select` field, keyed by option value. Label priority: choices[value].label, else the option's own `label`, else the raw value; `description` comes only from here. Keys that match no option are ignored; an option without a key falls back per that priority.

OptionSourceRef.doc: Choices for the field at `pointer`, loaded from .../runtime-forms/v2/:runtimeId/option-sources/:sourceId.

OptionSource.doc: Response of the option-sources endpoint. select: options + defaultValue. dependent_select: per-value lists keyed by the value of dependsOn. `customValueAllowed`, `status`, `reason` and `retryable` are sent only on the v2 endpoint and only to forms that list the matching capability (`select.custom_value`, `option_source.status`); a form without the capability gets the source exactly as before. Form-consistency parameter `?formRevision=<token>` (Definition.revision), optional, three outcomes: (1) absent — the source answers with the plain direct-option protocol and NEVER includes saved-connection options (Option.connectionId) or connection-keyed model maps, so pre-existing clients keep working unchanged; (2) present and matching the server's current build — the source answers within the capability range the form declared; (3) present and not matching — HTTP 409 with code `form_revision_stale` and recovery `refetch_form`; the client must refetch the whole form and must never merge new options into a stale form. The revision guards form consistency only; authorization and connection state are re-checked on every source request and again on save.

customValueAllowedByValue.doc: dependent_select only, keyed like optionsByValue. true with no listed options for that value: a free-text field (blank start). true with listed options: a combobox, as `customValueAllowed`, starting at defaultValueByValue. The server sends it only to a client that advertises `dependent_select.custom_value_with_options` (query `clientCapabilities`, comma-separated, on the definition, edit-form, option-source and submit requests; optional, never in requiredClientCapabilities); any other client gets that value list-only, as before the capability existed; the server decides how each value is stored (an unlisted typed one as a custom value; a listed one normally as a preset, though other fields may make it an override: Built-in Pi stores a listed OpenRouter model saved with a limit as a custom model). false/absent: pick from the list.

customValueAllowed.doc: capability `select.custom_value`; meaningful only for kind `select` (dependent_select keeps customValueAllowedByValue). true: render a combobox (pick a listed option or type a value). The server stores a listed value as a preset and an unlisted typed value as a custom value; a required field still needs a non-empty value. On edit, a stored value that is not in the list is shown and submitted as a typed value, never reported as not-a-choice.

status.doc: capability `option_source.status`. live: the list came from the Computer's probe. fallback: the probe was not live and the list is the bundled one (usable; show `reason`). unavailable: no list at all; `options` is []. One status per source, worst wins (unavailable > fallback > live), dependent_select included (there is no per-value status). A source-level failure is reported here, never as a form-level error, and never makes a client fall back to v1 (v1 fallback is only for a form-level 404 or protocol error). Client obligations: unavailable + required field: show the status and (when retryable) a retry, and block submit; unavailable + optional field: hide the field. Retry = request the same source again with `?refresh=1`; the server then asks the Computer again, bypassing its model-list cache (the Computer's probe gate already single-flights concurrent probes), and answers from its own last-good copy (`state: stale`) only when the Computer does not answer in time.

reason.doc: capability `option_source.status`. Why the status is not live; absent when status is live. probe_timeout and probe_failed stay distinct. Server mapping from the Computer's probe outcome: missing_config -> missing_config; no_models (or a live list with no models) -> no_models; unsupported -> unsupported; probe error with code detect_timeout, or the server's own wait timing out -> probe_timeout; probe error with code computer_offline, or the Computer offline/unrouted -> machine_offline; any other probe error or failure -> probe_failed. Clients must accept an unknown reason (show a generic message).

retryable.doc: capability `option_source.status`. Whether retrying may change the answer: true for probe_timeout, probe_failed, machine_offline and no_models (the user may add models); false for missing_config and unsupported. Absent or false when status is live.

state.doc: capability `option_source.status`; sent next to `status` and additive to it (a client that ignores it keeps the `status` rules). Present only when the Computer did not answer this request in time; absent when it answered, or when the server knows its state (offline). stale: the list is the last one it reported, received at `fetchedAt`; `status` is then `fallback` with reason `probe_timeout` (retryable), so a client that ignores `state` still shows a usable list with a retry. unavailable: the server has no earlier list; `status`/`reason` (probe_timeout) say what is shown instead. The server keeps waiting for the Computer in the background and caches a late answer, so a retry usually gets it. Clients must accept an unknown state (treat it as absent).

fetchedAt.doc: capability `option_source.status`. ISO 8601 time the server received the list shown with `state: stale`; absent otherwise.

unavailableOptions.doc: Additive; no requiredClientCapabilities entry. Options that exist but cannot be picked now, kept OUT of `options` so a client that ignores this field never offers them: models this Computer's runtime itself listed as disabled (never models from Raft's bundled catalog: when the Computer provides a list, that list alone decides), and on v3 also saved provider connections that are not selectable (disabled, missing credential; `connectionId` set). Render them after the listed options as a disabled, non-selectable group: by `group` when present (`saved`: the saved providers group), else "Not available on this computer"; never submit one as a new pick. v3: a current value equal to an entry shows selected-and-unavailable and blocks saving (`option_unavailable`), except on a source with `customValueAllowed`, where it is accepted as a typed value. A client that ignores the field loses only the hint. The server never accepts a value as listed because it appears here (a source with `customValueAllowed` still accepts any typed value, as before).

connectionId.doc: capability `provider.saved_connection`. Non-empty marks this option as a saved provider connection. Hard constraint: value === "connection:" + connectionId; an option violating it is a protocol error. Sent only to forms that declare the capability, and only when the request carried a matching formRevision. Display metadata (label, underlyingProviderId, providerKind) is never trusted back: on save the server re-resolves the connection by id in the current server scope.

underlyingProviderId.doc: capability `provider.saved_connection`. The connection's provider id (e.g. deepseek). Distinct from providerKind, which only carries preset/gateway semantics.

group.doc: capability `provider.saved_connection`. Display grouping: saved connections first ("Saved providers"), then direct/manual providers.

unavailable.doc: capability `provider.saved_connection`. Edit only: the agent's currently bound connection is not selectable right now (disabled, missing credential, retired). It stays visible, keeps the agent's stored value, and blocks save until the user picks something else — a silent rewrite never happens. v2 only: v3 sends such an option in OptionSource.unavailableOptions instead.

unavailableReason.doc: capability `provider.saved_connection`. Localized-safe reason key for `unavailable` (e.g. disabled, missing_credential, retired, not_found). v2 only.

UnavailableOption.doc: An option shown greyed in a select (OptionSource.unavailableOptions), never selectable as a new pick.

reason.doc: Why it is not available, as plain text: for a model, the runtime's own reason (untrusted runtime text, already trimmed and length-capped by the server); for a saved connection, server copy in the request language. Render as plain text only. Absent when there is no reason; the client then shows the disabled row without a description.

connectionId.doc: v3: set on a saved provider connection that is not selectable (value === "connection:" + connectionId).

underlyingProviderId.doc: v3: the connection's provider id, as Option.underlyingProviderId.

group.doc: v3: display group, as Option.group (`saved` for a connection).

protocolVersion.doc: 2 or 3 (the protocolVersion of the form the client rendered); formValues have the same semantics on both.

Submission.doc: The runtime-form part of POST /api/agents: field values keyed by dataSchema property name. The server assembles the runtimeConfig.

ConditionalRequired.doc: v3: one `dataSchema.allOf` entry (JSON Schema if/then/else limited to `required`).

if.doc: Condition schema over the whole values object (see Condition.schema).
